subject: battus-philenor
notes: On the pipevine by the gate.

identification.evidence: Dark/black dorsal coloration with distinct orange-red lateral and dorsal markings along the wing margins and pronotum edge — characteristic of Lygaeus kalmii. Oval, somewhat flattened true-bug body shape (Hemiptera), long slender antennae, and six slender legs visible. Size relative to human finger consistent with ~12–14 mm adult. Orange banding pattern along wing edges matches Lygaeus kalmii more closely than the large milkweed bug (Oncopeltus fasciatus), which has broader, bolder orange patches. Found on broadleaf vegetation in Chico, CA, well within the California range of L. kalmii.

Key visible features supporting this identification: (1) small, shield-shaped stink bug body (~5–7 mm) typical of Pentatomidae; (2) striking black-and-white/orange patterning with bold white spots and streaks on the dorsum — the diagnostic "painted" pattern of Bagrada hilaris; (3) orange-red transverse band visible across the abdomen/connexivum; (4) dark scutellum with white markings; (5) short, segmented antennae with alternating dark/pale banding; (6) found on what appears to be a ripe tomato in the Central Valley of California, consistent with the bug's known host range and invasive range in CA.
